AfterAutoPostPlayPhaseEntered.rationale: `if (Pile != null && Pile.Type == PileType.Exhaust && player == Owner) await CardCmd.AutoPlay(choiceContext, this, null)` (HowlFromBeyond.cs:32-39) == `if self in self.combat.player.exhaust_pile: self.combat.auto_play_card(self)`. The pile test, the self-target and the auto-play verb all match, and unlike card/havoc this one really does go through `CombatState.auto_play_card`, so the full play bracket runs (combat.py:516-556) -- including the pile removal that pulls it back OUT of the exhaust pile (combat.py:526-535, which explicitly lists `exhaust_pile` with a Howl From Beyond comment). The sim maps the AutoPostPlay phase to its end-of-turn auto-play slot, the same slot Stampede uses; the `player == Owner` clause is the multiplayer ownership gate. Note the card is NOT Exhaust-keyworded -- the Exhaust hover tip (HowlFromBeyond.cs:17) advertises the TRIGGER -- so it only replays when something else exhausts it, and the sim leaves `exhausts` False.

ctor.rationale: `base(3, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AllEnemies)` (HowlFromBeyond.cs:19-22) == cost 3 / ATTACK / UNCOMMON / ALL_ENEMIES.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(16m, ValueProp.Move)` (HowlFromBeyond.cs:15) == `_damage = 16`, powered on both sides.

OnPlay.maps_to: HowlFromBeyondCard.on_play, routed per-enemy by the framework (howl_from_beyond.py:78-81; combat.py:481-487)
OnPlay.issue: The damage and the single hit per enemy are faithful against `DamageCmd.Attack(16).FromCard(this).TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)` (HowlFromBeyond.cs:26-29), and leaving `handles_own_routing` False is correct for a one-hit AoE -- the framework filters on `is_gone` (combat.py:483-484), the right analogue of `where c.IsAlive`. ALL-ENEMIES FAN-OUT: C# passes the whole valid-target list to ONE `CreatureCmd.Damage(targets: validTargets)` call (AttackCommand.cs:650), which computes every DamageResult first and only then calls `await Kill(killedCreatures)` for the batch (CreatureCmd.cs:372-409); the sim issues a separate `DamageCmd.deal` per enemy, so each death resolves before the next enemy is damaged. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/conflagration's OnPlay entry (rule 3). DORMANT -- no ported Ironclad-reachable monster has an on-death effect that changes a sibling's incoming damage. Presentation, folded in: WithAttackerAnim("Cast") and WithHitFx.
